newsitem.title: MALI: Clashes in Mali ahead of poll.
newsitem.headline: Clashes in Mali ahead of poll.

text.p: Opposition supporters vowing to disrupt Sunday's rerun parliamentary election in the West African state of Mali ransacked and set fire to the national headquarters of the ruling ADEMA alliance, witnesses said.

Police and paramilitary gendarmes dispersed the attackers, who also ransacked the nearby townhall of the central district of the capital Bamako on Saturday night after a protest march by 3,000 opposition activists vowing to boycott the poll.
Mali was widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system.
The constitutional court scrapped the April 13 parliamentary poll citing organisational chaos.

The opposition wanted the whole election timetable revised but President Alpha Oumar Konare, a historian elected in 1992, pressed ahead with only minor modifications and won a May 11 presidential election -- also boycotted by the main opposition.
Almost 600 candidates from Konare's Alliance for Democracy in Mali (ADEMA), 18 other parties and 13 independent lists will contest the 147 national assembly seats on Sunday.
Polling starts at 8 a.m. (0800 GMT) and ends at 6 p.m. and some five million Malians are eligible to vote.
Konare's government has not formally banned protests but sources say that mixed patrols of police and gendarmes will take strict measures to ensure security during polling.
